title: Cross-team traffic choreography and snapshotting scratchpad (WIP)
content:
Purpose: scratchpad for a lightweight cross-functional pattern that combines deterministic traffic snapshotting with choreographed traffic choreography (slicing + staged activation). This is not the final playbook — it’s a working canvas to align product, SRE, and CS on how we snapshot live traffic, seed synthetic cohorts, and enforce telemetry contracts for safe canaries and small A/Bs.

High-level goals:
- Make small-exposure canaries reproducible and auditable (snapshot + replay anchors).
- Keep latency and cost SLOs predictable during staged exposure.
- Provide a clear decision lattice for escalation and rollback that teams can execute without deep runtime changes.
- Minimize observational blind spots by enforcing a minimal telemetry contract for every rollout.

Key concepts (quick definitions):
- Snapshot window: a deterministic sample (time-bounded) of production traffic metadata captured for comparison and Replay sanity checks.
- Choreography plan: ordered list of cohort activations, synthetic seed points, and guardrail checks.
- Telemetry contract: the minimum set of signals (latency P50/P95, error rate, model output entropy, user action conversion) that must be emitted pre- and post-exposure.
- Replay anchor: a small deterministic set of requests from the snapshot used to validate functional equivalence across model variants or routing changes.

Why snapshotting?
- Non-deterministic production traffic makes drift hard to attribute. Snapshots let us baseline an identical request set across runs (useful for investigating regressions in quality or cost).
- Snapshots + replay catch regressions in prefix-sensitive models and prompt-stateful features that live A/B slices can miss.

Operational pattern (steps, minimal viable):
1) Preflight (T-48h to T-1h):
   - Draft choreography plan and share with SRE, product, and oncall. Link: confluence:ROLL-1820-traffic-contracts.
   - Define snapshot window (default 30 minutes, low-traffic epoch). Include sampling seed and hash algorithm.
   - Record telemetry contract for the run. Minimum fields: request_id, user_cohort_tag, model_id, seq_len, prompt_hash, call_latency_ms, response_size_tokens, error_flag, score/confidence, top_3_outputs (hashes).
   - Enumerate privacy filters: drop PII fields, truncate long user text, keep one-way prompt hash.

2) Snapshot capture (T-1h):
   - Run deterministic sampler that writes to snapshot store (S3/Redwood internal blob) with metadata. Snapshot must be immutable and tagged by run_id, created_at, owner.
   - Take a quick smoke-run: replay 100 anchors locally against candidate model variant to catch obvious OOM/serving errors.

3) Synthetic seed & canary choreography (activation window):
   - Stage 0 (internal synthetic): Seed 1% of snapshot traffic via synthetic proxies to hit candidate model endpoints. Observe telemetry contract and signal drift.
   - Stage 1 (microcanary): Route 0.1% of live production traffic (prefiltered cohorts) + synthetic anchors. Hold 15–30 minutes.
   - Stage 2 (expanded canary): 1% of production traffic across orthogonal slices (region, browser, auth-state) for 1–2 hours.
   - Stage 3 (ramp): progressive increments with automated metric gates until target exposure.

4) Observability & gating (must-haves):
   - Telemetry contract enforcement: automated job validates contract completeness every 5m. Missing keys = immediate pause.
   - Gate metrics computed from both live and snapshot-replay results: latency delta, error delta, output-entropy delta, top-output-divergence (% different top-1), downstream conversion delta (if available).
   - Quorum rule: require at least 3 independent signals crossing thresholds before rollback auto-triggers (to avoid noisy single-signal flips). Example thresholds: latency P95 up +30%, error rate +1.0pp absolute, top-output-divergence >5%.

Decision lattice for failures (playbook sketch):
- Alert -> Pause traffic -> Triage -> Either immediate rollback OR degrade to next-best model variant -> Postmortem and snapshot attach.
- Triage steps: check replay anchors, compare snapshot vs live divergence, search for session-affecting prefixes, confirm infra/CPU/GPU metrics.
- Escalation timeline: first 10m -> runbook owner; 30m -> Eng lead; 2h -> Incident commander.

Telemetry contract (example schema snippet for engineers):
- request_id (string), prompt_hash (string), model_id (string), route_version (string), region (string), timestamp (iso8601), latency_ms (int), backend_cpu_util (float), tokens_out (int), error_code (nullable string), top1_hash (string), top1_confidence (float), output_entropy (float), cohort_tag (string).
- Storage: write to a dedicated experimental metrics table and to the snapshot blob (with redaction applied).

Synthetic proxies (why and how):
- Purpose: deterministic replays of snapshot anchors into candidate endpoints without affecting live users. Useful for debugging stateful/response-flaky models.
- Implementation notes: light-weight proxy service that can inject headers to mimic real users (auth-metadata redacted). Proxies should be rate-limited and run on dedicated canary GPUs when available.

Cost and capacity considerations:
- Budget the snapshot + replay run cost into the release ticket. Defaults: snapshot capture negligible; synthetic replay cost estimate = 0.01% of one production QPS per hour.
- If Dedicated pools are constrained, reduce synthetic seed or shorten Stage 1 hold time. Decision and fallback must be in choreography plan.

Cross-team responsibilities (short):
- Product: define target cohorts and success criteria, own downstream conversion checks.
- SRE/Infra: snapshot tooling reliability, quota exceptions, routing changes and emergency kill-switch.
- Applied ML / Model Owners: validate model variants against replay anchors, maintain model degradation matrix.
- CS/Support: prepare comms templates for customer-impacting rollbacks and postmortem summaries.

Preflight checklist (T-24h minimal):
- [ ] Snapshot window chosen & tagged
- [ ] Telemetry contract saved to run_id
- [ ] Privacy redaction confirmed by Security
- [ ] Synthetic proxy ready and smoke-tested
- [ ] Oncall schedule and pager rotations set with run_id in subject
- [ ] Cost estimate annotated in ticket

Things to validate during the run (sweeps):
- Snapshot replay consistency: 95% top-1 hash match allowed baseline for identical model family.
- Latency P50/P95 drift from snapshot replay vs live should be within configured latency budget percentage.
- Downstream success signals (conversion) may lag — plan backfilled checks at 24h/72h.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should snapshots be held for exactly X days? (privacy + storage cost tradeoff). Proposal: 7 days by default, extend to 30 days for enterprise audits.
- How to version snapshot hashing so it’s resilient to prompt normalization changes? Need stable canonicalizer in SDK.
- Auto-rollforward: allow auto-scale-down of model variant instead of full rollback for cost-induced regressions? (needs product decision)
- Integrate with Console’s rollouts UI: expose snapshot run_id, replay anchors and a small diff-view for top-output-divergence.

Quick notes from recent dry-run (2025-01-27):
- Synthetic anchors caught a tokenization mismatch between our tokenizer and a 3rd-party model adapter (saved ~2h of debugging).
- Missing top1_confidence in one stream caused gating job to pause — enforce schema presence early.

References and further reading:
- Internal: confluence:ROLL-1820-traffic-contracts, internal incident RR-2209 postmortem (search).
- External inspiration: paper on reproducible evaluation sets for web-scale systems; canary best-practices doc from X.

Notes for next iteration:
- Add small on-console UI mock for snapshot diffing (shows 10 anchors and side-by-side outputs).
- Draft an infra SLA for snapshot store durability and retention exceptions.
- Prototype a compact snapshot format with pre-hashed prompt + minimal context for privacy-first auditing.

Author notes: this doc is intentionally practical and ops-focused. Use it to align a single cross-functional pilot before we generalize into the full rollout playbook. Feedback welcome — especially on telemetry schema edges and the quorum rule thresholds.

Last edits: 2025-03-05 by Ava Martinez.
